name: SS Marquette & Bessemer No. 2 — Lake Erie Central Basin Search

target.last_known_position: Departed Conneaut, OH bound for Port Stanley, ON
target.conditions: Severe winter storm, gale force winds, heavy seas
target.status: Never found. Largest vessel lost on Lake Erie.

search_area.description: Lake Erie central basin, Conneaut-Port Stanley corridor
search_area.notes: Central basin max depth ~210ft. Wreck likely in 60-180ft range based on route.

debris_sightings: Life raft found near Long Point, ON
Bodies recovered near Erie, PA (east of route)
Wreckage reported near Conneaut harbor entrance

pipeline_steps.name: historical_research
pipeline_steps.description: Search for historical accounts, news articles from 1909-1910, debris sighting locations with coordinates

pipeline_steps.name: drift_analysis
pipeline_steps.description: Given debris sighting locations and December 1909 weather (SW gale), back-calculate probable sinking location using wind/current drift models

pipeline_steps.name: aeromagnetic_scan
pipeline_steps.description: Check USGS/NOAA aeromagnetic data for the probable search area. Steel hull (2514 tons) should produce strong dipole signature if data exists.

pipeline_steps.name: satellite_window_analysis
pipeline_steps.description: Analyze 15-year satellite archive (2010-2025) for optimal detection windows. Look for: post-storm clarity, low turbidity, calm surface. Lake Erie central basin is shallow enough for optical detection in clear conditions.

pipeline_steps.name: detection_scan
pipeline_steps.description: Run detection pipeline on best satellite tiles from the probable search area

notes: Step 1 must complete before step 2 (drift needs debris locations)
Steps 3 and 4 can run in parallel after step 2
Step 5 depends on both step 2 (bbox) and step 4 (best dates)
If no aeromagnetic data exists for the area, note it and continue
If drift analysis produces multiple probable zones, run steps 3-5 for each
Final report should include: probable sinking location(s), confidence levels, recommended survey areas, best detection windows
